issue.title: Command-mode sequences: mark with Ctrl+M, run in order
issue.description: In Bob Command Mode, Ctrl+M marks commands into an ordered sequence that Enter or Ctrl+Enter runs one at a time. The status-bar bob chip shows how many steps there are and which command is running. RECENT shows each past sequence as one row that runs it again.
issue.creation_reason: Approved epic plan plan:202610/command_mode_sequences.md requests this work

payload.entry: LAND AUDIT / FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE before remaining-work tale: Read the epic, all four children and every note, approved plan plan:202610/command_mode_sequences.md, plugins commits cdd61a4/a8f33a2/38da67d/af35d48 and CLI 3965f749, and actual engine/runner/plugin/chip/toast/pager/sheet source and tests. All three final decisions are implemented: attention continues, Escape clears marks, rerun-last replays the full sequence. Fetched origin/master matches CLI 3965f749 and plugins af35d48. Reviewed concurrent plugins 145ea37/458907b/4bb8821 (wikilinks), c391a0d (type ink), 4e31220 (Events caption), and CLI 4a95e5b7/e08f859f/4f29a824: no extra sequence caller, duplicate driver, or incompatible catalog/API change; Calendar stamp JSON is additive. Remaining epic defects: 177-sheet-sequence renderRow depends on ElementStub .classes/children.find/_listeners; real Chromium confirms plain click activates twice, Ctrl-click activates as well as marking, pending-mark clicks activate, badges/tint and RECENT separators/durations are missing. No-mark argument Shift+Enter incorrectly warns about sequences; marked Ctrl+Enter with a highlighted completion runs a single command and leaves marks. A RECENT sequence reduced to one mark uses row=null and bypasses report/preview/confirm UI. rebuildRows omits activeSequenceIds, so a running sequence is shown interrupted. Docs omit required summary actions, sequence chip/pager/record details and retain contradictory Escape/rerun-last text. These remain er work, not tasks. Repro artifact file:explicit:a0f49d2561ee189f6902ef4a. Fresh 158/158 command-mode tests, build:check, and validate 8/8 pass; full npm test 4544/4549, unrelated failures logged in file:explicit:e36d5e43c260c84cd22570ce. All PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1 entries triaged with sase_new_task: er.1 startup pair -> existing bob-cli-eh +1; er.2 startup pair -> same corroboration, keystroke perf -> causal active bob-cli-eq note; er.3 startup pair -> eh, snapshot/cold-growth perf -> eq note; er.4 startup pair -> eh, snapshot/rank -> eq note, unspecified nonrecurring fifth failure declined as a separate task for lack of node/reproduction. eq note also records current cold-chunk failure; isolated log file:explicit:c74e72c69664b05e05280be8 (3/5 passing, snapshot and rank still fail). Same-type/all-type searches and last-week task sweep found no matching perf task; closed bob-cli-3w is a different fixed dependency-stage node, not reopened. No new tasks. epic-symbols empty; no symvision recipe. No parent_bead. Epic remains open pending validated medium tale sase_plan_command_mode_sequence_closeout.md; coder must repair, run required gates including just check (never check-full), deploy, and close er plus mark original plan done in the same turn without waiting for its own commit. Full CLI/docs gates and repaired deploy remain with that coder.

Verified close of bob-cli-er. All four phases remain closed (er.1–er.4) with their notes and commits (plugins cdd61a4, a8f33a2, 38da67d, af35d48; CLI 3965f749). All three decisions remain implemented: attention continues, Escape clears pending marks before closing, Rerun last replays the whole stamped sequence. Catalog protocol 1, record schema 1 with optional stamp, and api.commandMode v1 are unchanged.

Concurrent drift rechecked at closeout: plugins origin advanced to 8ef763a (block-id-prompt picker layout/e2e; no command-mode file overlap; workspace fast-forwarded onto that SHA). CLI origin advanced through 45b8346d (gcal stamp spacing) and 3ca356c6 (task wikilink guide); neither touched docs/guides/run-bob-from-obsidian.md.

Repairs landed in 170-sheet.js and 177-sheet-sequence.js: a base handleRowClick hook with real-DOM classList/Array.from(children) rendering (no production _listeners); no-mark argument keys delegate to the original handler; marked Ctrl+Enter with a highlighted completion accepts then add-and-run; incomplete arguments leave marks and show Needs; a RECENT sequence reduced to one mark reconstructs via cmReplayRun and uses the original activateRow chain; rebuildRows passes live activeSequenceIds so a running sequence shows ⟳. Fragments stay under 1000 lines (170=912, 177=860). Chromium production-DOM coverage (TMPDIR=/tmp) plus 162/162 command-mode tests pass. Preview frames show marked rows, tray, review card, and RECENT sequences in light and dark.

Docs: plugin reference Sequences section after Command sheet; Escape clears marks then closes; chip N/M with title and sequence clock; pager step i of n; optional sequence stamp schema 1; CLI guide chip/summary and Rerun-last sequence sentence.

Gates: npm run build, build:check, command-mode 162/162, npm test 4558/4560, validate 8/8, npm run docs:check, just docs-check, sase tool run check af9ae8787cc20f122e77177b54a072e4 pass. The two npm test failures are the known ledger startup pair (note-ready linear storm; relationIndex layout-ready), corroborating bob-cli-eh, not sequence defects. Wikilink index performance remains bob-cli-eq. epic-symbols empty. just symvision recipe absent from the primary justfile.

Deploy: bob plugins sync --repo this checkout --no-pull -p bob-command-mode copied main.js from the uncommitted 8ef763a build. Unrelated overwrite refusals recorded and not forced: block-id-prompt, bob-ledger-tools, bob-navigation-hotkeys, task-status-cycler (other workspace uncommitted deploys). Live Obsidian was not reachable; Chromium production render/click coverage and preview frames were used instead.

Follow-up outcomes from the lander stand: er.1–er.4 startup pair -> bob-cli-eh; index/wikilink perf -> bob-cli-eq; unspecified er.4 transient declined (no node/reproduction). No parent_bead.
